title.value: OSSEM: ONE-SHOT SPEAKER ADAPTIVE SPEECH ENHANCEMENT USING META LEARNING
title.justification: The title directly states the core focus of the paper, which is the development of a speech enhancement system using meta-learning for speaker adaptation.
title.quote: OSSEM: ONE-SHOT SPEAKER ADAPTIVE SPEECH ENHANCEMENT USING META LEARNING

extractions.description: This paper presents a novel one-shot speaker-adaptive speech enhancement (SE) system called OSSEM, which utilizes meta-learning to adapt SE models efficiently to individual speakers with minimal data. The system combines a modified transformer SE network and a speaker-specific masking network, intending to improve SE in various speech applications. The proposed approach is trained using a modified Voice Bank-DEMAND dataset, enabling real-time enhancement while maintaining competitive performance with existing systems. OSSEM's architecture and training techniques are designed to optimize fast adaptation and stability.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper is centered around enhancing speech processing systems through deep learning techniques, specifically focusing on speaker adaptation using meta-learning. While this might have indirect implications on communication technologies, it does not directly address climate or ecological sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: The goal of speech enhancement (SE) is to improve the quality and intelligibility of distorted speech. In various speech-related applications, such as automatic speech recognition, speaker recognition, and assistive hearing devices, SE serves as an indispensable front-end unit.

primary_category.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on advancing techniques in speech enhancement through deep learning and meta-learning. It does not primarily address any climate or ecological sustainability issue.
primary_category.quote: In this study, we propose a novel meta-learning-based speaker-adaptive SE approach (called OSSEM) that aims to achieve SE model adaptation in a one-shot manner.
